title: observability-telemetry-scenarios-and-dashboard-narratives
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a scenario-driven planning note for telemetry we need to instrument around inference pipelines and operator-facing dashboards. The goal is to produce compact, narrative-centered dashboard surfaces that answer common operator questions quickly and map cleanly to traces when deeper investigation is needed.

Scope:
- Metrics and trace anchors for token serving, KV cache behavior, routing/fallbacks, and tenant isolation signals.
- Dashboard narratives (operator stories) for runbook-first investigation flows.
- Lightweight sampling and retention strategy recommendations to balance query cost and diagnostic fidelity.

Why narratives?
Operators don't start with metrics names; they start with a story: "why are requests slow for tenant X right now?" Dashboards should be organized as a set of 3–5 investigative narratives, each with a clear lead metric, 2–3 supporting slices, and a trace anchor.

High-level investigative narratives (examples):
1) Tenant Slowdown (per-tenant SLO breach)
   - Lead metric: tenant_p99_request_latency_ms (quantile)
   - Supporting slices: kv_cache_hit_rate_by_model, request_queue_depth, model_variant_fallback_rate
   - Trace anchors: span:inference.request -> attributes: tenant_id, model_name, route_policy, cache_state
   - Quick hypothesis checklist: capacity contention (queue depth), cold KV cache (low warmth), routing fallbacks (higher cost model).

2) Token Surge Cost Spike
   - Lead metric: token_cost_rate_usd_per_minute (derived)
   - Supporting slices: average_tokens_per_request, batch_size_distribution, replicate_calls_per_request
   - Trace anchors: span:tokenizer -> span:runtime.generate with attribute token_count and kv_cache_hit boolean
   - Action: surface top-10 tenants by token consumption and recent prompt templates via prompt_signature metric.

3) Model Regression (quality + latency anomaly after rollout)
   - Lead metrics: model_response_quality_regression_ratio, model_p95_latency_ms
   - Supporting: function_call_error_rate, hallucination_detection_alerts, rollout_canary_error_delta
   - Trace anchors: span:model.invoke + span:postprocess with attributes: rollout_tag, canary_percent, eval_prompt_id

Core metric definitions (compact, operator-friendly):
- request_count: count(inference.request) incremental per request (tagged by tenant_id, route, model_name).
- request_latency_ms: duration between inference.request.start and inference.request.end (ms). Aggregates: p50/p95/p99.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: kv.cache_hits / (kv.cache_hits + kv.cache_misses) (tags: model_name, tenant_id, cache_tier). Note: compute as rate over 5m windows.
- queue_depth: instantaneous queued inference calls per executor pool (tags: pool_id, region).
- model_variant_fallback_rate: fraction of requests that were routed to fallback variants (tags: primary_model, fallback_model).
- tokens_per_request: token_count attribute on inference.request (compute avg/median/quantiles).
- token_cost_rate_usd_per_minute: derived from tokens_per_request * pricing_lookup (for hosted/dedicated differentiation).
- trace_sampling_rate: per-tenant configurable sampling (see sampling section).

Span naming and attribute conventions (tracing anchors):
- span names: inference.request, tokenizer.encode, runtime.generate, kv.cache_lookup, kv.cache_warm, model.invoke, postprocess.normalize, routing.resolve
- required attributes (all spans where applicable): tenant_id, request_id, model_name, route_policy, seq_len, token_count (for tokenizer/runtime.generate), kv_hit (boolean for kv.cache_lookup), gpu_node_id, batch_id, rollout_tag
- lightweight span payloads: avoid embedding full prompts in spans; instead surface prompt_signature (hash) and optionally short_prompt_excerpt (first 200 chars) when enabled for debugging.

Dashboard composition: narrative -> lead widget -> supporting slices -> trace jump links
- Lead widget: single KPI with change sparkline and immediate context (current vs baseline). Example: tenant_p99_request_latency_ms with baseline p99 for last 7d.
- Supporting panels (3): heatmap of latency by model and route, kv_cache_hit_rate trend, request queue per pool.
- Top-10 table: top tenants by latency/cost with direct trace links (trace id TTL marker).
- Drilldown affordances: clicking on a tenant row should open pre-populated investigation query (trace time window + tenant filter + span focus).

Sampling strategy (recommended):
- Default: 0.5% trace sampling globally to keep costs predictable.
- Elevated sampling: 10% for requests that hit latency p95/p99 thresholds or hit fallback variants.
- Per-tenant overrides: enable 5–25% sampling for high-traffic customers during incidents via feature flag.
- Full-capture policy: ephemeral full capture for 5–20 minutes triggered by runbook automation when a confirmed SLO breach is detected. Capture includes first-party spans and anonymized short_prompt_excerpt.

Retention tiers and query cost control:
- High-detail traces: 7 days (full spans) for sampled traces.
- Aggregated metrics and span indices: 90 days.
- Long-term compressed traces (span index only, no payload): 365 days for billing/forensics.
- Query throttle knobs on dashboards: limit time window to 1h by default; require explicit confirmation for >24h dense queries.

Query examples (pseudo-SQL/PromQL-ish):
- p95 latency by model: quantile_over_time(0.95, request_latency_ms{model_name=~".*"}[5m])
- kv hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses[5m]))
- fallback rate: sum(rate(model_fallback_count[5m])) / sum(rate(request_count[5m]))

Dashboard UX heuristics (practical):
- Always surface baseline and percentage delta. Operators want context, not raw numbers.
- Prefer heatmaps+sparklines over stacked timeseries for high-cardinality signals.
- Reduce panel count: 6–9 maximum per narrative dashboard to keep scrolling minimal.
- Each panel includes "jump to trace" and "open query" actions with prefilled filters.

Ownership and alerting tie-ins:
- Each lead metric must map to an owner (oncall team or model owner). Ownership metadata should be visible in UI.
- Alert definitions should be tied to the narrative: who to page, what runbook to execute, suggested mitigation steps.

Lightweight instrumentation checklist (developer facing):
- Add tenant_id and request_id to inference.request root span.
- Emit kv.cache_hit boolean on kv.cache_lookup spans.
- Emit approx_token_count on tokenizer.encode and runtime.generate spans.
- Tag routing decisions with route_policy and fallback_model when used.
- Emit queue_depth gauge from executor pool exporter every 10s.

Operator play examples (runbook-first):
- Scenario: p99 latency spike for tenant T
   1) Open "Tenant Slowdown" narrative, filter tenant=T.
   2) Check lead KPI and 7d baseline.
   3) View queue_depth panel — if >threshold, throttle or scale pool.
   4) Check kv_cache_hit_rate -> if < warm_threshold, trigger cache-warm job or temporary bypass.
   5) If fallback_rate increased, rollback recent rollout or route to fallback variant.
   6) If still unknown, click top trace link and inspect spans for model.invoke time and batch sizes.

Unresolved questions / design tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Prompt hashing: which hash to use to balance reproducibility and PII safety? SHA256 of normalized prompt? Need guidance from security.
- Sampling cost model: what is the expected monthly cost of 10% elevated sampling for top 50 tenants? @Miguel to run a sizing estimate (JIRA-OPS-987).
- How to surface model quality signals (hallucination, function-call failures) without losing signal-to-noise? Define a compact quality index.

Next steps / action items:
- (Asha) prototype a Tenant Slowdown dashboard wireframe in Grafana + link generator for trace jumps (due 2024-12-01).
- (Miguel) cost estimate for sampling policies and retention tiers (due 2024-11-20).
- (Dana) security review for prompt_signature design and short_prompt_excerpt policy (due 2024-11-15).
- Run a 2-week pilot enabling elevated sampling for 5 high-traffic tenants and gather operator feedback.

Notes: this doc is meant to drive a 1-hour workshop with eng-observability + SRE + product-hosted-api to decide on the initial narrative set and sampling defaults. Bring examples of dashboards and live queries.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-ONBOARD-1234 (telemetry conventions)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood/telemetry/PR-452 (span attribute extractors)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-987 (sampling cost analysis)

End of doc.

---
Working style notes (informal):
- This is intentionally conversational; add more concrete metric names as we standardize.
- If you edit this doc, prefix your name and date for traceability.
summary: Scenario-driven observability planning note: narratives, lead metrics, trace anchors, sampling & dashboard UX heuristics.
